title: Question Improvement Program — Sections B/C/D Quality Elevation

include: Priority: formula-only stems > definition-driven > weak-context > other
Prefer topics naturally supporting judgment, recommendation, or tradeoff analysis
exclude: Items with CognitiveLevel: Analyze or Evaluate (88 items)

candidates_evaluate.rationale: Stem already asks 'Should this be investigated?' but reduces to formula comparison (5% of $150K = $7,500). Elevate to multi-factor investigation decision: materiality, trend, controllability, and cost-benefit of investigation.
Pure plug-and-chug ($18 x 2 DLH x 8,000 = $288,000). Elevate to scenario: evaluate whether to use permanent staff vs. temporary labor given seasonal demand, overtime premiums, and training costs.

candidates_evaluate.topic: Transfer pricing — minimum price with excess capacity
candidates_evaluate.rationale: Already has decision context (excess capacity, market vs. variable cost). Elevate to full evaluation: should the selling division accept the internal transfer at variable cost, negotiate a split of savings, or sell externally? Multiple stakeholder perspectives.

RI = $450K - ($3M x 10%) = $150K. Pure formula application. Elevate to: evaluate a proposed investment that increases operating income and assets — compute impact on RI and recommend whether the division manager would accept it, contrasting RI vs. ROI incentives.

$197,500 / 625 x 23 = $7,268. Pure ABC formula. Elevate to: given plant-wide vs. ABC cost assignments for two products, evaluate which method better reflects resource consumption and recommend pricing changes for a product that appears profitable under traditional costing.

CM = $80 - $50 = $30. One-step subtraction. Elevate to: a special order at $60/unit with $200K incremental fixed costs — evaluate whether to accept, considering capacity constraints, strategic implications, and qualitative factors.

BE = $252K / ($84-$56) = 9,000 units. Formula application. Elevate to: evaluate product launch decision by comparing expected demand distribution to break-even, assessing downside risk, and recommending go/no-go with sensitivity analysis.

candidates_analyze.rationale: 'Which time series component represents long-term direction?' Pure definition. Elevate to: given five months of sales data, analyze which time series components (trend, seasonal, cyclical, irregular) are present and recommend the most appropriate forecasting method.

candidates_analyze.topic: Static vs. flexible budget — cost control evaluation
candidates_analyze.rationale: 'Which budget should be used to evaluate cost control performance?' Single-select. Elevate to: given static budget, flexible budget, and actual results, analyze cost control performance by computing and interpreting the static budget variance and flexible budget variance separately.

($50K + $60K) / 2 = $55K. Simple average. Elevate to: given sales data with trend + seasonality, analyze whether a 2-month, 3-month, or weighted moving average is most appropriate — explain why each method over/under-reacts to the pattern.

Compute price variance ($4.80 actual vs. $5.00 standard). Elevate to: analyze both price and quantity variances together — the purchasing manager bought cheaper material that led to higher usage. Which manager is responsible? Analyze the tradeoff.

Rate variance = ($19-$18) x 2,100 = $2,100 U. Efficiency variance = (2,100-2,000) x $18 = $1,800 U. Elevate to: analyze the relationship between rate and efficiency — paying higher wages for more skilled workers, is the efficiency gain worth it? Analyze the net effect.

($5.50-$5.00) x 800 = $400 U. Extremely short stem (91 chars), pure calculation. Elevate to: analyze the purchasing manager's decision — the price increase was due to an emergency rush order to avoid a production shutdown. Analyze whether the variance should be investigated and who bears responsibility.

$920K - $690K = $230K. Simple subtraction. Elevate to: given margin of safety for two product lines with different cost structures, analyze which product is riskier, how changes in fixed cost structure affect the margin, and what it implies for strategic planning.

$500K / 100K = $5.00 per DLH. Extremely short stem (56 chars). Elevate to: analyze whether DLH, machine hours, or ABC activity drivers is the most appropriate allocation base for a highly automated plant vs. a labor-intensive plant — analyze the cost distortion each base would produce.
